node.title: Re: readdir() on a sysopen() handle?
node.author: afoken
node.doctext:
Looking through several linux man pages, it looks like you normally should use [man://opendir], [man://readdir] or [man://scandir], and [man://closedir] from C. Those functions are specified by POSIX and are portable. But the glibc also offers [man://fdopendir] that converts a plain integer file descriptor to a DIR *. So in C, something like this should work:

/* UNTESTED! */ DIR * d opendir_nofollow(const char * pathname) { int fd = open(pathname, O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW); if (fd == -1) { return NULL; } return fdopendir(fd); }

Converting that to a perl directory handle will very likely require a little bit of XS code. Perhaps [mod://Inline::C] might be helpful. You definitively want to have a look at the perl sources, the part that implements the [doc://opendir] function, to see how to correctly create a directory handle.

Alexander

--
